messages:
alex: FYI saw two OOMs on prod-gpu-pool at ~13:24 UTC, both during very long chat sessions (>12k tokens). Memory spike correlates with KV cache growth. :eyes:

maria: Copy — can you paste the serve log + runtime trace? Any recent kernel or batching rollouts?

alex: log snippet: `OOM at kv_alloc.cpp:482` then `fallback to spill` but it failed to free quick enough. No recent config changes on that pool.

jin: quick thread — we pushed a kernel-selection heuristic last week that prefers the new fused-attn kernel for 2048+ seq to cut latency. That kernel uses a different KV layout and a transient pinned staging buffer during recompute. Could be related.

sam: interesting — batching heuristics also adjusted: we increased max_batch_tokens to 65k for high-throughput to reduce per-token overhead. Long single-user contexts + larger batch token cap => more KV cached entries retained.

alex: attaching short flame: ``
  cpu: 12%
  gpu_mem: 14.9G -> 18.0G (spike)
  kv_cache_entries: 4.1M -> 7.3M
``

tara: if kernel change adds transient pinned buffers we might hit host->dev staging pressure and prevent timely eviction. Can we repro on staging with a long-context workload?

jin: repro steps I ran locally:   
``
# simulate long convo + high batching
python bench_longctx.py --seq-len 12k --batch-token-cap 65000 --model redwood/v1-large
```
produces sustained kv_alloc growth until OOM. I captured profiler: ``KV: alloc growth 0.9MB/step; pinned staging peaks at 1.2GB``

maria: good repro, thanks. Short-term mitigation for prod? Rollback kernel heuristic or force KV eviction policy to be more aggressive on longctx shards.

sam: ops suggestion: change runtime config for prod-gpu-pool to `kv_cache.eviction_threshold = 0.6` and `batching.max_batch_tokens = 32000` to limit in-flight KV. That should reduce headroom pressure.

alex: rolling a non-disruptive change now to the pool: `kv_cache.eviction_threshold=0.6` + enable `kv_cache.watermark_based_eviction=true`. Deploy-bot will run the rollout.

deploy-bot: deploy started by alex for pool=prod-gpu-pool, cfg_changes=[kv_cache.eviction_threshold, kv_cache.watermark_based_eviction, batching.max_batch_tokens]. Canary on 2 nodes. :rocket:

jin: FYI we should also add a temporary fallback mode: if kv_alloc rate > X for N steps, serve engine should switch to shortctx-mode (drop long KV reuse, prefer windowed context) to avoid OOMs. I can prototype today.

tara: agree — graceful degradation > rollback. Prototype API: `runtime.set_fallback('shortctx', condition={kv_rate: 0.8MB/s, duration: 30s})`

maria: also adding alert rule: kv_cache_memory_growth > 500MB in 1m for any node => P1 with auto throttles.

sam: change applied to prod canary. Monitoring shows mem spike ceiling flattened; no new OOMs in last 12 min on canary hosts.

alex: great. Followups: jin to prototype fallback, jin+tara to add unit/integration test for pinned staging buffer accounting, maria to add alert and runbook edits, sam to monitor full rollout. I'll open a follow-up ticket. :thumbsup:

jin: timeline: prototype today, tests tomorrow, canary-ready fallback by EOD Friday.

maria: added runbook note: when OOM with kv_alloc stack -> check kernel-selection flag `fused_attn_pref` and `batching.max_batch_tokens`, consider quick rollback to safe kernel.

alex: closing this thread once rollout completes and no OOMs after 1h on full pool. Thanks everyone. :heart:
